stories.title: AP Braces for Cyclone, Odisha Issues Red Alerts, 9 TN Ports on Alert
stories.summary: According to the IMD, the system is very likely to cross the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam around forenoon on October 28

article_sentences: A brewing cyclone in the Bay of Bengal threatens to unleash a spell of dangerous weather across the South Peninsula, with isolated extremely heavy rainfall exceeding 20 cm forecast over Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal, and Kerala and Mahe over the next two days.
Coastal Andhra Pradesh and Yanam are in the firing line on Tuesday and Wednesday, with Telangana also bracing for heavy rain on Wednesday.
The bigger threat, however, lies along the Andhra Pradesh coast, where a very severe cyclonic storm is expected to make landfall by Wednesday.

Squally weather, gale-force winds and rough to very rough seas are forecast over the western and central Bay of Bengal from Tuesday, with the impact spilling over to the Andhra Pradesh and adjoining Odisha coasts.
Explaining the evolving threat, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said a well-marked low-pressure area over the Bay had intensified into a depression by Sunday morning, as anticipated.
It had slowed to a crawl, moving at just 5 km/hr over six hours before virtually stalling over the south-east Bay of Bengal at 5.30 am.

The depression lay about 440 km north-northwest of Sri Vijaya Puram in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands; and 880 km east-southeast of Visakhapatnam, 980 km east-southeast of Kakinada, 1,080 km east of Machilipatnam and 1,150 km east of Bapatla, all along the Andhra Pradesh coast.

The system is forecast to initially turn nearly southwards before strengthening into a deep depression and gradually recurving west-northwest over the east-central and adjoining south-east Bay later on Sunday.
It is expected to intensify into a cyclone over the east-central and adjoining west-central Bay on Monday, and further into a severe cyclonic storm by Tuesday morning.
The storm is then likely to turn northwestwards, gathering strength as it bears down on the Andhra Pradesh coast.
By Wednesday morning, it could become a very severe cyclonic storm, crossing the coast between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam, along with Yanam, later that forenoon.
Maximum sustained winds of 115–125 km/hr, gusting to 140 km/hr, are forecast at landfall.

stories.headline: Schools shut, shelters readied: Odisha, Andhra, Tamil Nadu gear up for cyclone
stories.title: Schools shut, shelters readied: Odisha, Andhra, Tamil Nadu gear up for cyclone
stories.summary: Schools shut, shelters readied: Odisha, Andhra, Tamil Nadu gear up for cyclone
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Odisha has intensified cyclone preparedness ahead of a potential October 28 landfall on the Andhra Pradesh coast.
Schools will remain closed in five districts, while rescue teams and shelters are ready as the IMD forecasts heavy rainfall and strong winds.

The Odisha government has stepped up preparations to deal with a potential cyclone, deploying rescue teams and preparing evacuation shelters as a very severe cyclonic storm is expected to make landfall along the Andhra Pradesh coast on October 28.
Meanwhile, Puducherry has been receiving continuous rainfall since last night as the weather system over the Bay of Bengal intensifies.
The well-marked low-pressure area over the central and adjoining southeast Bay of Bengal intensified into a depression on October 24 and subsequently developed into a cyclonic system.
Cyclone warning signals have been hoisted at nine ports in Tamil Nadu, including Chennai, Nagapattinam and Cuddalore, following the intensification of the weather system over the Bay of Bengal.

According to the India Meteorological Department (IMD), the depression is likely to move northwestwards and intensify further, becoming a very severe cyclonic storm over the west-central Bay of Bengal off the Andhra Pradesh coast by the morning of October 28.
Although the storm is forecast to cross the Andhra Pradesh coast, southern and coastal districts of Odisha are likely to experience heavy rainfall and strong winds.
Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi has directed officials to prioritise public safety, evacuation and emergency response, with the objective of ensuring zero casualties.

According to the India Meteorological Department (IMD), a depression over the Bay of Bengal is likely to intensify into a very severe cyclonic storm and cross the Andhra Pradesh coast between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam by the forenoon of October 28.
The system is expected to bring maximum sustained wind speeds of 115-125 kmph, with gusts reaching 140 kmph.
The storm is expected to make landfall around 300 km from Gopalpur in Odisha, officials told PTI.

stories.title: Cyclone to cross Andhra coast on October 28; people in low-lying areas from Bapatla to Vizianagaram to be evacuated
stories.summary: Andhra Pradesh may witness light showers on October 25 and 26, while much of the cyclone-induced rainfall activity likely to begin on October 27
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The weather system in the Bay of Bengal is likely to strengthen into a very severe cyclonic storm and cross the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam by the forenoon of October 28, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said on Sunday (October 25, 2026).
Winds of 115 to 125 kmph, gusting to 140 kmph, are expected when it crosses the coast.
At 5.30 a.m. on Sunday, the system was a depression about 880 km east-southeast of Visakhapatnam, 980 km from Kakinada, 1,080 km from Machilipatnam and 1,150 km from Bapatla.
The IMD expects it to become a cyclonic storm by Monday (October 26) morning and a severe cyclonic storm by the morning of October 27, before it heads north-west towards the coast.
The Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority (APSDMA) has begun preparing for the landfall.
Its Managing Director, Prakhar Jain, told.
The Hindu that people living in low-lying areas and kutcha houses in the coastal districts from Bapatla to Vizianagaram would be evacuated to shelters.
He said the impact was expected in Bapatla, Krishna, West Godavari, Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Konaseema, Kakinada, Anakapalli, Visakhapatnam, Vizianagaram and Srikakulam districts.
Not much impact was expected in Tirupati and SPSR Nellore districts, he said, adding that more clarity would emerge after the cyclone formed on Monday.
Andhra Pradesh has 12 battalions of the State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) and seven of the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) and the State has asked for three more NDRF battalions.
Even as the low-pressure area over the Bay of Bengal became well-marked on Saturday, Andhra Pradesh did not record any major rainfall activity on Saturday (October 24).
Only two districts, YSR Kadapa and Anantapur, received widespread moderate showers on Saturday.

stories.headline: Op Sindoor proved no target beyond IAF's reach; air power remains India's primary responder: Air Chief Marshal AP Singh
stories.title: Op Sindoor proved no target beyond IAF's reach; air power remains India's primary responder: Air Chief Marshal AP Singh
stories.summary: New Delhi, Oct 25: The Indian Air Force's calibrated strikes across the Western front during Operation Sindoor -- spanning 1,200 km in breadth and 200 km in depth--demonstrated that no target is beyond its reach, Chief of Air Staff Air Chief Marshal AP Singh said on Sunday, in an apparent warning to Pakistan. In an exclusive interview with PTI, the Air Chief described the operation as a validation of the IAF's capability-centric approach, emphasising that it reaffirmed air power's decisive role as both the nation's primary responder and its strategic deterrent. At the same time, the IAF Chief cautioned that validation of the IAF's approach must not be a reason to "stand still" as the way forward is to deepen and widen this capability across the force. "Operationally, one lesson stands out: we must always retain multiple options and the ability to adapt rapidly as the adversary changes tactics," the Chief of Air Staff who oversaw the four-day operation said. "A capability-centric force is inherently better at this, because it can draw on many tools rather than depend on one. That same flexibility allowed us to calibrate our response and keep control of escalation," he said. Launched in response to the Pahalgam terror attack, Operation Sindoor saw India carry out precision strikes against terror infrastructure in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied territories in May last year-- marking the most daring cross-border military action by the country since the 1971 Bangladesh Liberation War. "Operation Sindoor proved that the path we have chosen is the right one. We will continue along it with even greater resolve, so that if the nation calls upon us again, the IAF responds more swiftly, more precisely and more decisively, on the nation's terms," he said. The Chief of the Air Staff also noted that some of the indigenously developed weapons systems performed "exceptionally", delivering crippling blows deep into enemy territory, and that the IAF honoured its commitment to "zero collateral damage" throughout the operation. "Operation Sindoor was, above all, a validation of the capability-centric approach the IAF has been pursuing. We have moved from thinking in terms of individual platforms to thinking in terms of capability, where every aircraft, sensor, weapon and network is integrated so that the combined effect is far greater than the sum of the parts," the IAF Chief said. "The operation put that philosophy to the test in real operations, and it delivered. It reaffirmed the decisive role of air power as both the nation's primary responder and its strategic deterrent, and it reinforced the enduring importance of speed, precision, integration and adaptability," he said. The Air Chief Marshal was responding to a question on the IAF's key takeaways from Operation Sindoor across operational tactics, strategic options, setbacks, and firepower. The operation's success did not come from any single weapon or platform. It came from the combined effect of accurate intelligence, networked operations, stand-off and precision weapons, electronic warfare, layered air defence and counter-UAS (Unmanned Aerial Systems) capabilities, all working as one system, he said. "On the offensive side, calibrated targeting across the entire front, spanning 1,200 km in breadth and 200 km in depth, made it clear that no place is beyond the IAF's reach," he said. "Some of our indigenously developed weapons performed exceptionally, delivering crippling blows deep into enemy territory, and we honoured our commitment to zero collateral damage throughout," he said. The Chief of the Air Staff said India's home-grown networked air defence defeated the large number of drones and stand-off weapons launched by the Pakistan military as the nation could act with confidence. "Offence and defence reinforced each other, which is precisely what a capability-centric force is designed to achieve," he said. Air Chief Marshal Singh said Operation Sindoor also demonstrated the value of joint and multi-domain integration, adding bringing together the air, land, maritime, space, cyber and electromagnetic domains enabled faster decision-making and greater operational effect. The IAF Chief, however, said the force must now focus on strengthening combat mass, ISR (intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance) prowess, electronic warfare, counter-UAS capability, resilient networks and AI-enabled decision support. "Equally, we must build the ability to sustain high-intensity operations over time through robust logistics, maintenance, infrastructure and, above all, indigenous production. Work is already under way on each of these fronts. Air Chief Marshal Singh said the IAF's vision is closely aligned with the larger national vision of Viksit Bharat 2047, as a developed India must also be a secure and resilient India. "The Defence Forces Vision 2047 likewise envisages an integrated, multi-domain and technologically advanced military in support of this national ambition," he said. For the IAF, the Chief of Air Staff said it means evolving into a multi-domain aerospace force capable of protecting India's growing economic, technological and strategic interests across the entire spectrum of conflict. "We have set out a clear, structured path towards that goal. The IAF's Capability Perspective Plan-2047 lays down long-term priorities based on emerging technologies, and it feeds into ten-year plans that are updated periodically," he said. In the space domain, the Air Chief Marshal said the broader direction is reflected in the IAF Space Vision 2047. "Our emphasis will be on 'Aatmanirbharta', advanced aerospace technologies, artificial intelligence, autonomous systems, space, cyber, precision weapons and resilient networks. Just as important, we will build the industrial ecosystem needed to sustain all of these capabilities," he said. The IAF Chief argued that a secure India creates the environment for economic growth, while a technologically and economically stronger India provides the foundation for greater strategic power. "Realising this vision will require a whole-of-nation approach, and the IAF is committed to playing its full part," he said. "By 2047, we aim to be one of the world's most capable, innovative and technologically self-reliant aerospace forces, a force that stands as both the guardian and a driver of a developed India," he noted.

stories.headline: Congress cites former Supreme Court judge’s memoir; questions independence of judiciary under Modi government
stories.title: Congress cites former Supreme Court judge’s memoir; questions independence of judiciary under Modi government
stories.summary: Jairam Ramesh shared a media report which quoted the pre-publication manuscript of Justice Kaul’s memoir ‘Without Fear of Favour’ as stating that former Chief Justice of India Justice D.Y. Chandrachud was “too deferential to the Government” when it came to appointments
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence

event term: 'chief justice' in summary weight 25.2
event term: 'chief justice of india' in summary weight 27.6
article_sentences: Citing former Supreme Court judge Justice Sanjay Kishan Kaul's yet-to-be-released memoir, the Congress on Sunday (October 25, 2026) flagged "serious questions" regarding the independence of the judiciary under the Modi government and asserted that the institution tasked with upholding the Constitution must remain free from the pressures of those in power.

Congress general secretary in-charge communications Jairam Ramesh shared a media report which quoted the pre-publication manuscript of Justice Kaul's memoir 'Without Fear of Favour' as stating that former Chief Justice of India Justice D.Y. Chandrachud was "too deferential to the Government" when it came to appointments.

In his post in Hindi on X, Mr. Ramesh said, "A book by former Supreme Court judge Justice Sanjay Kishan Kaul has raised serious questions regarding the independence of the judiciary during the tenure of the Modi government."

Justice Kaul highlights several concerning incidents — government interference in the appointment of judges, attempts to secure government approval prior to Collegium meetings, and the government's absurd questioning regarding the caste of a judge belonging to a minority community, Mr. Ramesh said.
Matters that many were previously hesitant to discuss openly have now been documented by Justice Kaul with measured, deliberate language, Mr. Ramesh said.
"Strikingly, a former Chief Justice of India (CJI) has not denied that discussions with the government take place prior to judicial appointments.

When former CJI Justice Chandrachud acknowledges that the government engages with the CJI and plays a role in the appointment process, the concerns surrounding judicial independence become even more profound," Mr. Ramesh said.

Equally grave is Justice Kaul's revelation that, after a Bench he presided over raised the possibility of reconsidering certain aspects of a court ruling in a PMLA (Prevention of Money Laundering Act) case, the matter was reassigned to a different bench without any consultation with him, he said.
"This points to the extent of the government's day-to-day interference in the functioning of the Supreme Court," Mr. Ramesh said.

"When there is pressure to obtain government approval for judicial appointments, and when benches hearing sensitive cases are altered, one must ask — in the interest of safeguarding democracy — if this does not constitute pressure on the judiciary and an erosion of its independence, then what does?" the Congress leader said.
"The institution tasked with upholding the Constitution must remain free from the pressures of those in power.
In a democracy, the independence of the judiciary is not merely an option; it is an absolute necessity," Mr. Ramesh asserted.

stories.headline: As COP31 nears, India’s heatwave disaster tag puts spotlight on global adaptation finance gap
stories.title: As COP31 nears, India’s heatwave disaster tag puts spotlight on global adaptation finance gap
stories.summary: India’s move to classify heatwaves as disasters spotlights a widening gap in international adaptation funding, with experts warning that developing nations face a finance shortfall far beyond current flows as COP31 approaches.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: As India officially recognised heatwaves as natural disasters nearly three months ahead of the UN climate change conference (COP31) in Türkiye, officials and experts have pointed out that the move exposes a stark reality of a global climate finance system that pushes vulnerable nations to pay for immediate climate survival entirely on their own.

“This task would have been much simpler if we had a good amount of international assistance that allowed us to access funds for various heat adaptation measures,” Krishna S Vatsa, National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) member and Head of the Department, told PTI Videos in an interview.

Stressing that the resources available for adaptation are “inadequate and unpredictable", Vatsa emphasised the need to improve access to the right kinds of technologies, including those required for efficient cooling.

According to India's first Adaptation Communication to the UN Climate Change Summit in 2023 (COP28), the country alone estimated a cumulative need for expenditure for adaptation of ₹56.68 lakh crore by 2030.
Adaptation finance refers to the funds spent to help communities prepare for and survive the unavoidable impacts of climate change.
The Indian government’s economic survey data 2025 shows that 98 per cent of India's adaptation finance is sourced domestically.
The gap between what developing countries need to adapt to a hotter world and the money that actually reaches them is expected to resurface at COP31 in Antalya.
“In terms of both finance and technology, we are at a disadvantage.
Heat is a very important concern for us, and therefore we decided to address the impacts of heat with our own national and state disaster mitigation funds.
We would definitely like to encourage states to develop heat action plans and implement them on the ground,” the NDMA HoD told PTI.
Vatsa underscored that international adaptation finance can complement national efforts and make a significant difference to the scale and speed of implementation.
Sustained support for a long-term adaptation strategy would be helpful and for that, steady, predictable, and consistent access to finance is a prerequisite, he added.
